cluster.family_skeleton: one class of person named as the driver of a crime trend, with the three measurements of that trend never put on the same page

members.headline: Immigrants Cut Victimization Rates, Boost Crime Reporting (Policy Analysis No. 1003)
members.note: Verbatim title from content/sources.json (en-cato-pa1003). NCVS 2017 to 2023: immigrants 44 percent less likely to be violently victimized. Publication day not recorded at snapshot.

members.headline: Comparing crime rates between undocumented immigrants, legal immigrants, and native-born US citizens in Texas (DOI 10.1073/pnas.2014704117)
members.note: Verbatim title from content/sources.json (en-pnas-light-2020). Texas arrest data 2012 to 2018, a different population and a different instrument from the Cato study, which is exactly why the two are shown side by side rather than averaged.

members.headline: FBI Releases 2024 Reported Crimes in the Nation Statistics
members.note: Verbatim title from content/sources.json (en-fbi-2024-crime). Violent crime down an estimated 4.5 percent and murder down 14.9 percent in 2024 against 2023. Release day not recorded at snapshot, so the date carries the year only.
